# Traces (neatlogs)

Status when this was written (11 October 2026): **nothing was created in neatlogs and no trace id could be looked up.**

- The neatlogs MCP server did not connect in the session that did task T05. The session's start-up report gave HTTP 503
  ("503 Service Temporarily Unavailable") from the server's endpoint, and a second look for its tools in the same session found none.
  So `get_detection_capabilities`, `preview_detection`, `create_detection`, `search_traces` and `get_trace_context` were never reachable
  and were not called. The brief's stop rule (stop if the preview fails twice) was not reached; there was no preview to fail.
- No committed run file stores a trace id (`runs/*/run.json` has no trace field), so there is nothing to copy from the runs.
- The detection "Model answer needed a repair call" is therefore not created. For reference, the program already knows this failure:
  `crossfoot/model.py` `ask_json` sends one repair request after an answer that is not valid JSON or fails its check, but it records no
  event for that request (only a final refusal as `page_failed`), so a detection would have to match on the span for the second call of a
  pair, not on a ledger event.

To finish later: reconnect the server, list its detection capabilities, preview on two or three recent trace ids, create the detection,
and write its name, id and preview matches here with the trace ids of the committed runs and how to open one
(`search_traces`, then `get_trace_context` with `limit` 5).
# Recovery evidence

## A run stopped by its budget and continued

Two small counties (San Saba, Cottle), real model calls, run 20261011-135519 (`runs/20261011-135519/`). Ledger events and
the counts come from `runs/20261011-135519/ledger.sqlite` and `summary.json`. Evidence ids are in `.prod-build/evidence.jsonl`.

1. `crossfoot audit --all --only san_saba,cottle --budget 0.25` (E0071, exit 2, expected)
   - Last lines of the run's summary: San Saba `audited` (33 calls, $0.2076); Cottle `stopped`: "run budget $0.25 reached
     (estimated spend $0.2573 after 39 calls); refusing the next call". "1 of 2 counties closed."
   - Ledger after the stop: San Saba 1,100 cells, 1,100 accepted, 21 page reads, `read_done` written. Cottle 168 cells read from 3
     pages, 0 accepted, no `read_done`.
2. `crossfoot audit --all --only san_saba,cottle --resume 20261011-135519 --budget 2` (E0072, exit 0)
   - Last lines: "san_saba skipped: closed in the run being continued"; "cottle end: audited; 21 calls, $0.1944, 95.5 s";
     "2 of 2 counties closed; model calls 61; metered cost (estimate) $0.4626".
   - Ledger after: San Saba still 1,100 cells, 1,100 accepted, 8 re-read tries, 21 page reads (unchanged: no page of it was
     read again). Cottle 664 cells, all accepted, 12 pages.

Counts: model calls San Saba 33 (first run only; the resume added none), Cottle 7 in the first run plus 21 in the resume = 28,
all 61 in the run. So nothing accepted was read again. What was paid twice: Cottle's three half-read pages (7 calls, about $0.06)
were read again from the start, because a county whose read did not finish is read whole again (its half-read cells are cleared,
none of them had been accepted). Gateway's own figure for the two commands: $9.9109 to $10.1791, then to $10.3736.

## Where a read failed and what the program did next

Quoted from the events kept in the committed runs' `county.json` files. Times are the event clock (UTC, as the runs record it).
Neatlogs trace ids are not given: see `docs/evidence/traces.md`. No run file stores a trace id, and the neatlogs server did not answer
in the session that wrote this.

### 1. A re-read gave the same value and went one step up the ladder, and the document disagreed with itself

Run `20261011-112935` (`crossfoot close --county panola --resume latest`), `runs/20261011-112935/panola/county.json`, item
`col:6:p6-b3:1` (page 6, the small total under precinct 1's column):

    11:29:58 suspect   read 1079, would_be 1076 (the three cells above add to 1076)
    11:30:01 reread    claude-sonnet-4.6, 400 dpi, ladder_step 0: old 1079, new 1079, kept "same"
    11:30:01 check     ok false, computed 1076, printed 1079, failing_in_block 2
    11:30:04 reread    claude-opus-4.6, 400 dpi, ladder_step 1: old 1079, new 1079, kept "same"
    11:30:04 check     ok false, computed 1076, printed 1079, failing_in_block 2
    11:30:04 verdict   document_inconsistent: "the scan shows 1079 there on every re-read (claude-sonnet-4.6 read 1079,
                       claude-opus-4.6 read 1079) while both sums it sits on still fail ... The document disagrees with itself."
    11:30:04 item_end  document_inconsistent

The first re-read agreed with the first reading, so the program asked a stronger model at the same size (one step up) and got the
same value; two readers and two failing sums ended it as `document_inconsistent`. No value was changed.

### 2. A value that ended `cannot_verify`

Same run, item `row:1:reg:REGISTERED` (the registered-voters row on page 1; its cells add to 17923, the printed total reads 17921):

    11:30:04 item_start
    11:30:12 reread  claude-sonnet-4.6, row total, 400 dpi        11:30:12 check ok false, computed 17923, printed 17921
    11:30:19 reread  claude-sonnet-4.6, row strip, 400 dpi        11:30:19 check ok false, computed 17923, printed 17921
    11:30:35 reread  claude-opus-4.6, row strip, 500 dpi          11:30:35 check ok false, computed 17923, printed 17921
    11:30:40 reread  claude-opus-4.6, row total, 500 dpi          11:30:40 check ok false, computed 17923, printed 17921
    11:30:54 reread  claude-opus-4.6, row strip, 400 dpi          11:30:55 check ok false, computed 17923, printed 17921
    11:30:57 reread  claude-opus-4.6, row total, 400 dpi          11:30:57 check ok false, computed 17923, printed 17921
    11:30:58 verdict cannot_verify: "six actions used on this item and its sum still fails"
    11:30:58 stop / item_end cannot_verify

Six actions, then the program stopped rather than loop. The cells stayed as read, marked `cannot_verify`.

### 3. A model answer the program refused

Run `20261011-130414` (`crossfoot audit --all --budget 9`), `runs/20261011-130414/scurry/county.json`, Scurry page 18:

    13:28:47 page_failed  page 18, error: "y" of 'REP John Bailey' must be a number from 0 to 1000

This is the case the runs record: a model answer that parsed as JSON but failed the program's checks. The model client asks once more
for a corrected answer before giving up (`crossfoot/model.py`, `ask_json`), and the repair request is not an event of its own, so the
runs hold the final refusal only; no event in the committed runs records an answer that was not JSON at all. What the program did next:
the page was left unread and listed (the rest of the county went on: pages 16, 17 and 19 were read at 13:28:32 to 13:28:47), then the
validator was changed (`hackathon.md`, T04d) and `crossfoot read-page` read page 18 into a copy of the ledger: in
`runs/20261011-141015/scurry/county.json`, `14:09:58 page_read page 18, PRECINCT 10, claude-haiku, 64 cells, 8 contests`.

# Traces (neatlogs)

Written 11 October 2026 (task T05b; it replaces the T05 note that said the neatlogs server did not answer). The server answered.
Everything below was read from the neatlogs MCP server with `search_traces` and `get_trace_context`, and from `runs/*/run.json` (start times).
Dollar costs are not given: neatlogs reports cost 0 for every trace here.

## How to open one

1. `search_traces` with a word that appears in span text (`read_group`, `read_page`, `reread`, `choose_reader`, `san_saba`, `crossfoot`; limit up to 100).
   Each result has `trace_id`, `start_ts`, `root_span_name`, `span_count`, `total_tokens`.
2. `get_trace_context` with the full 32-character `trace_id` and `limit` 5 (the options `span_types`, `span_names`, `fields`, `max_chars_per_field`
   answer `not_enabled`). Add `include_evaluations: false` to keep the answer short.
3. No run file stores its trace id. A run is paired to a trace by its start time (`run.json` `started`, UTC) against the trace's `start_ts`

## Two traces opened with `get_trace_context`

- `6b289ce0c777683ca054674468c29dbd` (cottle, the resume of run 135519): 15 spans, 7 model calls. First spans: `read_county` (workflow, 81.0 s), root `cottle`,

  `image WxH sha256:...`: it is a `neatlogs_media` record with `state: failed` and `safe_preview: "upload unavailable: backend_upload_contract_unavailable"`
  (png, 455,204 bytes, sha256 `57094643...`). The same appears in the close trace `af57604a...`: some images show as `image WxH sha256:...` and others as this failed record.
  The span's `read_page` input/output was empty; the page number is in the model's answer text only (here the precinct "401").

## The detection

- Name: **Crossfoot slow haiku call (over 20 s)**; id `ee3ce3bc-f2cc-44f6-aecb-387ebfdb3727`; kind: conditional; group Neutral; runs on spans of type LLM.
- Rule: `latency > 20000` ms AND `model = claude-haiku`.
- Why this one: the brief's first two choices could not be written. (a) A `reread*` tool span has an empty output; the value read is on its child model span, and
  "the value changed" is not on any span. (b) The repair request is not recorded as a span of its own (`crossfoot/model.py` `ask_json`). (c) a slow model call is on the span (`latency`, `model`).
  I did not change `crossfoot/tracing.py`.
- Preview (`preview_detection`, 14-day window, once): **1 span matched**, nothing else. The match: span `13de33922ba4b1e1`, a `claude-haiku` call whose input is the
  close-county planning prompt for "page 4, block p4-b6, Presiding Judge, Court of Criminal Appeals ... failing sum: row EARLY" and whose answer was `Action: reread ... row_total ... EARLY ... 400 ... claude-sonnet-4.6`.
  It is a planning call, not a page read, so the name says "haiku call" and not "read". I did not look up which trace holds that span, so no trace id is given for the match.
- Created with `create_detection`: the server answered "Detection created. A 14-day backfill is running"; `backfill_status` was `pending`. Whether it is active was not
  re-read with `list_detections` after creation, so "active" is the server's creation answer, not a second check.
